t: You're in Trevor Square, an elongated garden square in Knightsbridge. It was designed in the 1810s, chiefly by the architect William Fuller Pocock. The houses along its two long sides were built in the 1820s, with slate mansard roofs, and they are listed. The square is named after Sir John Trevor, a Welsh lawyer and politician who was Speaker of the House of Commons and Master of the Rolls. His second term as Speaker ended over a bribery allegation, and he was expelled from the Commons soon after.
